title: When the Rivergate Breaks
premise: Zephyrine Vane, a nonbinary salvage diver and estranged child of the late archaeologist Dr. Odile Vane, has spent years drifting between dig sites, taking cash work and never signing anything. When a government survey team vanishes near Rivergate Sound—leaving their gear intact, their boat anchored, and no tracks in either direction—Zephyrine is the only local who can read the tides well enough to find them. The search leads to a sunken colonial wreck that Odile had secretly located before her death, one holding documents that could return stolen land to the Rivergate community. Racing a licensed salvage fleet that will bury the evidence under legal ownership claims, Zephyrine must choose between disappearing again and claiming the inheritance—and belonging—they've spent a lifetime outrunning. They surface with the proof, the missing surveyors alive, and, for the first time, a reason to stay.
about_author: Tamsin Joubert is a former maritime surveyor who spent a decade charting coastal wrecks before turning to fiction full-time. Their novels are known for tidal pacing, salt-bitten prose, and protagonists who trust water more than people.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Working a cash dive job at Rivergate Sound, Zephyrine finds an abandoned government survey boat—gear stowed, kettle warm, no people. The harbormaster offers a finder's fee; the salvage fleet offers more to stay quiet. Zephyrine takes neither but starts reading the currents alone. Emotional beat: restless competence curdling into reluctant responsibility—the pull of a mystery they'd rather not care about.

chapters.title: What Odile Left in the Mud
chapters.summary: Alternating Zephyrine POV with recovered journal entries from Dr. Odile Vane. Following anomalous sonar readings from her mother's old notebooks, Zephyrine locates the wreck beneath the survey team's last known position—and realizes Odile found it first, then hid it deliberately. The salvage fleet arrives early, armed with a court injunction. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing as anger; the dawning truth that her mother's secrecy was protection, not rejection.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, with interludes from the trapped surveyor Maren Kole. Diving through collapsing hull sections on falling tides, Zephyrine reaches the surveyors alive in an air pocket and recovers the land-grant documents proving Rivergate's stolen title. But the fleet's crew seals the wreck entrance behind them, betting the tide will solve its own problem. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve—justice outside the law demands someone willing to drown for it.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Using Odile's tide tables, Zephyrine leads the surveyors out through a blowhole channel on the sixth tide's slack water, surfacing into a harbor full of Rivergate townsfolk who blocked the salvage ships' departure. The documents go public; the injunction collapses; the fleet withdraws. Offered a permanent post mapping the sound, Zephyrine unpacks a bag kept packed for eleven years. Emotional beat: quiet arrival—stopping no longer costs more than staying.
